data.ruling:
The refutation stands. For "function requirements: FUNCTION", the check at tools/research/round1.js:266 asks whether the function's requirement list names every requirement that IOBoard.md, the answers and the values found for research set for that function, with no value weaker than theirs. IOBoard.md sets two values on the RP2354B that the claim's 30 entries do not name.

(1) PIO instruction memory. IOBoard.md:259 says the state machines of one block share "that block's 32 instructions of memory", and P5 counts it beside the state machines. IOBoard.md:233 needs 64 of the 96 instruction words for bidirectional DShot on all 4 multiprotocol ports. The claim's "PIO" entry takes 3 blocks, 12 state machines and the GPIO base of 0 or 16 from :107. It does not take the 32 instructions a block. No other entry names it. The instruction memory is a resource of the microcontroller, just like the 12 state machines the list does carry, so it is a requirement on this function.

(2) Maximum input-low level of 0.8 V at IOVDD 3.3 V. The idle-bias row at IOBoard.md:256 cites build 2024-08-08, Table 1433. It relies on the line held at 0.34 to 0.79 V being "below the 0.8 V maximum input-low level". The R1 row of Research.md:279 makes R1 confirm "the pin ratings and pad figures the specification cites from build 2024-08-08", and names Table 1433 (1436 in build 2025-07-29) among them. The claim's "logic level" entry asks only for 3.3 V logic. The claim takes the pad pull-up from the same table and leaves out the input-low level.

Either omission alone is enough. It matches the T2 precedent: adjudicator-R1-3 let a refutation stand for the missing 520 kB SRAM. The fault is in the list, not in the part. The RP2350 datasheet, build 2025-07-29, re-read here, gives 32 instructions of memory for each PIO block and a maximum VIL of 0.8 V at IOVDD 3.3 V, so the RP2354B meets both. The scope is function: the finding is about what this function's requirement list must carry. It is not about the part's lifecycle, an end-of-life notice, the maker allowlist or its LCSC identity. The other entries were not found weaker than their sources, and this ruling does not depend on them.
data.evidence:
IOBoard.md:259 (PIO instruction memory, required): "the programs of all the state machines in one block share that block's 32 instructions of memory, and P5 counts it beside the state machines ... a bidirectional DShot port takes 16 words and a block holds at most 2 bidirectional DShot ports".

IOBoard.md:233: "Bidirectional DShot on all 4 takes 8 of the 12 PIO state machines and 64 of the 96 instruction words".

IOBoard.md:107 (PIO reach): "a PIO block sees 32 GPIO from a base of 0 or 16 ... 3 blocks, 12 state machines". This is the only source of the claim's PIO entry, which reads "3 PIO blocks of 4 state machines, 12 in all; a block sees 32 GPIO from a base of 0 or 16".

IOBoard.md:256 (Idle bias on an output line): "A 10 kΩ connector-side pull-down against that pull-up holds the line at 0.34 to 0.79 V, below the 0.8 V maximum input-low level", with the source "RP2350 datasheet, build 2024-08-08, Table 1433".

Research.md:279 (R1 row): "It confirms the pin ratings and pad figures the specification cites from build 2024-08-08 ... The pad pull-up of 32 to 86 kΩ and the input leakage are in Table 1433 (Digital IO), which is 1436".

The claim's "logic level" entry reads only "every signal that reaches an RP2354B pin is at 3.3 V logic, IOVDD at 3.3 V". None of its 30 entries names 32 instructions a block, 96 instruction words, or VIL.

tools/research/round1.js:266 gives the rule: "whether the function's requirement list names every requirement set for it by IOBoard.md, the answers and each value found for research ... with no value weaker than theirs".

RP2350 datasheet, build-date 2025-07-29, SHA-256 2877d0f270fb6d6a57943bee58aaad536aa027bea1e5b1c4ce2541a3230d4be8:
- PIO block diagram, chapter 11: "Instruction Memory / Write only / 32 Instructions / 4 Read Ports" (text line 66238).
- PIO example comment: "Each PIO instance has a 32-slot instruction memory" (line 66485).
- Table 1436, Digital IO: "Input Voltage Low VIL IOVDD=3.3V -0.3 0.8 V" (lines 101096-101125).

Precedent: results T2/019-adjudicator-R1-3.json let the refutation stand for the missing 520 kB SRAM, with scope function.
